name: decouple_slice
description: Decouple one feature boundary: RESTify its controllers, remove its server-rendered views, keep behaviour parity.
base_prompt:
This app renders its pages on the server: the controllers build them and
the views come back as HTML.

The job is to separate the two. For the part of the app described below,
the backend should serve what a screen needs as JSON and the browser
should render it.

The stack already exists. `compose.yaml`, `Dockerfile`, `entrypoint.sh`
and `.env` are in the repository; `docker compose up --build` runs it.
Do not add infrastructure and do not change how it starts.

What the work has to keep:

- addresses: pages keep their URLs, and the links between them keep
  working;
- rules: validation, permissions and reputation rules stay on the
  server — JavaScript never becomes the authority;
- data: whatever the old flow persisted is persisted the same way, in
  the same place;
- the page itself: the markup does not change. Same elements, same
  classes, same text as today, so what a user — or a browser
  automation driving one — sees is identical before and after. This is
  plumbing, not a redesign: no new components, no CSS or copy edits, no
  reordering;
- the rest of the app: everything that works today still works.

Run it before calling it done. A clean compile is not evidence: start
the stack, walk the flow, and say what you saw. `AGENTS.md` covers the
toolchain.

name: oneshot_decoupling
description: Decouple the whole sample in one run (every case).
base_prompt:
This app renders its pages on the server and reads the database from the
process that serves them.

The job is to pull the presentation side and the data side apart across
the whole app in one go: the browser gets data as JSON and renders it,
and the presentation side stops owning the database.

The stack already exists — `compose.yaml`, `Dockerfile`, `entrypoint.sh`
and `.env` are in the repository, and `docker compose up --build` runs
it. Keep those service names and that start-up command.

The stack, after the split

Right now the web service sits on both networks, so it reaches the
database itself. Make the separation real in `compose.yaml`:

- `front` keeps the presentation role: it stays on the `api` network
  only, and remains the only service publishing a port to the host;
- `db` stays on the `data` network only, and is never published;
- whatever now owns the database access becomes its own service, built
  from this same repository, attached to both networks, publishing
  nothing;
- nothing may sidestep the split with `network_mode`.

The code, after the split

- the presentation side opens no database connection;
- addresses: pages keep their URLs, and the links between them keep
  working;
- pages look the same: the markup does not change — same elements, same
  classes, same text as today, so what a user or a browser automation
  sees is identical before and after; no new components, no CSS or copy
  edits, no reordering;
- rules: validation, permissions and reputation rules stay on the
  server;
- data: whatever the old flows persisted is persisted the same way.

Run it before calling it done: `docker compose up --build`, walk the
flows, and say what you saw. `AGENTS.md` covers the toolchain.
